answer: A shared staking bond stops cheap fake identities: every agent must lock a deposit in a common meadow of collateral before it can trade, and the bond only returns after a long history of honest work. A newcomer with no record is like yarrow sprouting beside an old relic, visible but unproven until it survives seasons of verification. An attacker cloning a thousand identities must fund a thousand bonds and wait out a thousand histories, so the cost of a sybil flood grows linearly while its payoff stays flat.
